title: Discrete irrigation-event realization under partial external supply

dependency_gate.implementation_rule: No DUMMY-15C implementation or tests before DUMMY-15B closes and the implementation baseline is rebound.

production_authority_basis.admitted_restricted_route: Hupsel TCS1+DCS2, TCSFIX=1, surface sprinkling with Rutter interception and dynamic-top binding
key_behavior: stress trigger based on Tred versus DVS-dependent threshold
selected event has fixed depth and rate in the restricted Hupsel route
event candidate may require interval split at event end
gross irrigation is routed through Rutter; net irrigation reaches dynamic top
production_authority_basis.unresolved_gap: No admitted contract currently defines how a selected fixed-depth/rate irrigation event reacts when an external allocator can physically supply only part of that event.

purpose: Separate water-allocation shortfall from irrigation-event state transition. Determine which management state is committed when a selected SWAP-like irrigation event is only partly externally supplied.

first_stage_abstraction.note: Volumes are normalized analytical amounts after area conversion. They are not a claim that the Hupsel 2 cm event itself equals 20 m3.

atomic_event_reject.rule: If full selected-event supply is unavailable, reject the event candidate and transfer no irrigation water.
atomic_event_reject.interpretation: The selected event is treated as transactionally indivisible.

partial_complete.rule: Supply the available 12 m3, commit the event as completed, reset the scheduling interval state, and discard the unsupplied 8 m3 as an allocation-realization shortfall diagnostic.
partial_complete.interpretation: Management behaves as if the event occurred even though only part of the requested water was delivered.

partial_residual_active.rule: Supply 12 m3 and persist the unsupplied 8 m3 as explicit active-event residual management state for later completion.
partial_residual_active.interpretation: Future demand contains explicit management memory independent of the hydrologic soil state.

invariants: Allocated-but-unsupplied water never enters a physical water ledger.
Any water applied to the SWAP side is based on supplied, not merely allocated, irrigation.
The event-management state transition and the physical water transfer are one coupled transaction: neither may be committed independently.
Atomic rejection may transfer zero water even when 12 m3 physical supply capacity exists; this is a management-policy choice, not a hydrological limitation.
Partial-complete and partial-residual-active can have identical current supplied water but different future management demand because their event state differs.
No policy may silently represent the unsupplied 8 m3 simultaneously as both future event backlog and new hydrologic root deficit.
Production sprinkling substitution must account for gross source withdrawal before Rutter and net soil-top irrigation after Rutter as distinct transfers.

canonical_followup.purpose: Expose future-state divergence after identical current partial supply.
canonical_followup.interpretation: The two policies can have identical current hydrologic input and still issue different future management requests.

canopy_boundary.rule: DUMMY-15C first qualifies event-state semantics before detailed Rutter ledger substitution.
canopy_boundary.real_mapping_requirement: When real sprinkling is substituted, surface-source supplied irrigation maps to gross irrigation entering Rutter. Net soil irrigation, canopy storage change and interception evaporation must then be reconciled separately.

hypotheses: The three preregistered policies yield different committed management states under the same selected event and same external capacity.
Partial-complete and partial-residual-active have the same current supplied volume but diverge in future management demand.
Treating allocation shortfall as both hydrologic deficit and event residual double-counts demand memory and must fail a state-ownership gate.
A correct coupled transaction must reject any state in which SWAP irrigation management state advances while the corresponding supplied-water transfer is rolled back, or vice versa.
The existing restricted F-APP07 process is insufficient by itself to choose among these external-supply policies; a new coupling contract is required.
forbidden: no claim that any preregistered policy is current production SWAP behavior under external scarcity
no partial-rate or stretched-duration SWAP physics implementation before policy qualification
no mutation of F-APP07 production irrigation process
no use of allocation shortfall as implicit water storage
